items.title: The real Coxeter form, its radical, reflections, and form-preserving maps
items.statement:
Let $S$ be a finite set and let $m$ be a Coxeter matrix on $S$, so that $m(s,s)=1$ and $m(s,t)=m(t,s)\in\{2,3,\dots\}\cup\{\infty\}$ for $s\ne t$ ([[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]]).

**(1) The space and its distinguished functions.** Let $V:=\mathbb R^S$ be the real vector space of all functions $S\to\mathbb R$, with pointwise operations ([[def-function-space]]); it is a vector space over the ordered field $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-reals-ordered-field]]). Write $u(s)$ for the value of $u$ at $s$ and put $e_s(s):=1$, $e_s(t):=0$ for $t\ne s$.

**(2) The Coxeter form.** For finite $m(s,t)$ put $c(s,t):=\cos(\pi/m(s,t))$ ([[def-sine-and-cosine-by-power-series]], [[def-pi-via-first-positive-cosine-zero]]) and for $m(s,t)=\infty$ put $c(s,t):=1$; then $c(s,t)=c(t,s)$ and $c(s,s)=\cos\pi=-1$. The **Coxeter form** $B$ is the unique symmetric bilinear form on $V$ with $B(e_s,e_t)=-c(s,t)$ for all $s,t\in S$; in particular $B(e_s,e_s)=1$ and $B(e_s,e_t)=-\cos(\pi/m(s,t))$ for finite $m(s,t)$, while $B(e_s,e_t)=-1$ when $m(s,t)=\infty$ ([[def-bilinear-symmetric-skew-and-alternating-forms]], [[thm-bilinear-forms-correspond-to-linear-maps-into-the-dual]]). **No positive definiteness, definiteness or nondegeneracy of $B$ is presumed**: $\operatorname{rad}(B):=\{u:B(u,v)=0\text{ for all }v\in V\}$ may be nonzero ([[def-matrix-radicals-rank-and-nondegeneracy-of-a-bilinear-form]]), and the form may be indefinite ([[def-definiteness-inertia-and-signature-data-over-the-reals]]). A linear map $g:V\to V$ is **$B$-preserving** when $B(gu,gw)=B(u,w)$ for all $u,w\in V$.

**(3) Reflections.** For $a\in V$ with $B(a,a)\ne0$ define the **reflection with normal $a$** by $$r_a(v):=v-\frac{2B(v,a)}{B(a,a)}a .$$ The definition asserts neither that $r_a$ is linear or an involution nor that $\ker B(-,a)=\{v:B(v,a)=0\}$ is a hyperplane; these are proved in [[lem-cg-reflection-form-invariance-and-rank-two-orders]]. When $B(a,a)=0$ the symbol $r_a$ is not defined.
items.strategy: A definition item; the only substantive assertions are the bilinearity and uniqueness of $B$ and the elementary basis property of the $e_s$. Since $S$ is finite, $\sum_s\lambda_se_s=0$ evaluated at $s$ gives $\lambda_s=0$, so the $e_s$ are independent, and $u=\sum_su(s)e_s$ is a finite sum, so they span; hence a bilinear form is determined by its values on pairs of basis vectors, and the correspondence between bilinear forms and linear maps $V\to V^*$ ([[thm-bilinear-forms-correspond-to-linear-maps-into-the-dual]]) together with the basis property supplies existence and uniqueness of $B$; both facts are restated as the opening clause of [[lem-cg-reflection-form-invariance-and-rank-two-orders]], which is this definition's recorded justifier. Symmetry of $B$ follows from $m(s,t)=m(t,s)$ and from $c(s,t)=c(t,s)$; the diagonal value is $B(e_s,e_s)=-\cos(\pi/1)=-\cos\pi=1$ ([[thm-quarter-turn-values-and-shift-formulas]] is the companion record of $\cos\pi=-1$; the sine/cosine definition items fix the functions). The reflection formula is a definition of a vector $r_a(v)\in V$ for each pair $(v,a)$ with $B(a,a)\ne0$; linearity and the reflection identities are deliberately not asserted here and are established by the justifier. The page's central warning is preserved: no Euclidean structure, positive definiteness or invertibility of the Gram matrix is presumed. No Choice is used: $S$ is finite and all selections are finite.

items.title: Reflections: involutivity, form invariance, fixed hyperplane, and exact rank-two order
items.statement:
Let $S$, $m$, $V=\mathbb R^S$, $B$ and $r_a$ be as in [[def-cg-real-coxeter-form-and-reflection]].

**(1) Well-definedness of $B$.** The functions $e_s$ ($s\in S$) form a basis of $V$, and there is exactly one symmetric bilinear form $B$ on $V$ with $B(e_s,e_t)=-\cos(\pi/m(s,t))$ for finite $m(s,t)$ and $B(e_s,e_t)=-1$ for $m(s,t)=\infty$; it satisfies $B(u,w)=\sum_{s,t\in S}u(s)w(t)B(e_s,e_t)$ for all $u,w\in V$.

**(2) Reflection identities.** Let $a\in V$ with $B(a,a)\ne0$. Then $r_a$ is linear, $r_a^2=\mathrm{id}_V$, $r_a(a)=-a$, $r_a(v)=v$ for every $v$ with $B(v,a)=0$, and $B(r_au,r_aw)=B(u,w)$ for all $u,w\in V$. Moreover $\ker B(-,a)$ is a linear subspace of dimension $\dim V-1$ (a hyperplane of $V$, in the codimension-one sense) and is fixed pointwise by $r_a$.

**(3) The rank-two plane.** Let $s\ne t$ in $S$, put $P:=\mathbb Re_s+\mathbb Re_t$ and $c:=c(s,t)$ as in [[def-cg-real-coxeter-form-and-reflection]] (so $c=1$ when $m(s,t)=\infty$). Then:

(i) $B|_P$ has Gram matrix $\begin{pmatrix}1&-c\\-c&1\end{pmatrix}$; for finite $m$ it is positive definite, with $B(x_se_s+x_te_t,\,x_se_s+x_te_t)=(x_s-cx_t)^2+\sin^2(\pi/m)\,x_t^2$; for $m=\infty$ it is positive semidefinite, i.e. $B(x,x)\ge0$ for all $x\in P$, with radical $\mathbb R(e_s+e_t)$.

(ii) $r_s$ and $r_t$ fix every element of $P^\perp=\{v\in V:B(v,e_s)=B(v,e_t)=0\}$ pointwise; and if $m<\infty$ then $V=P\oplus P^\perp$.

(iii) The product $A:=r_sr_t$ has, in the ordered basis $(e_s,e_t)$ of $P$, the matrix $A=\begin{pmatrix}4c^2-1&-2c\\2c&-1\end{pmatrix}$, of determinant $1$.

(iv) If $m<\infty$ then $\operatorname{tr}A=2\cos(2\pi/m)$, $A^m=\mathrm{id}_V$, and $A^k\ne\mathrm{id}_V$ for $0<k<m$. If $m=\infty$ then $A=\mathrm{id}_P+N$ on $P$ for some $N$ with $N\ne0$ and $N^2=0$; hence $(r_sr_t)^k|_P=\mathrm{id}_P+kN$ for every $k\in\mathbb Z$, so $r_sr_t$ has infinite order on $V$.
items.strategy:
(1) Use the basis argument of the definition item: independence and spanning of the $e_s$ for finite $S$, then bilinear extension, i.e. [[thm-bilinear-forms-correspond-to-linear-maps-into-the-dual]] applied to the linear span of the prescribed basis values. (2) For $v\mapsto B(v,a)$ linear, $r_a$ is a linear combination of $\mathrm{id}$ and the rank-one map $v\mapsto B(v,a)a$, hence linear; $r_a(a)=a-2a=-a$; $r_av=v$ whenever $B(v,a)=0$; and $r_a^2=\mathrm{id}$ because $B(r_av,a)=B(v,a)-2B(v,a)=-B(v,a)$, so applying the formula twice reverses the coefficient of $a$ twice. Form invariance is the expansion $B(r_au,r_aw)=B(u,w)- rac{2B(u,a)B(a,w)}{B(a,a)}- rac{2B(w,a)B(a,u)}{B(a,a)}+ rac{4B(u,a)B(w,a)}{B(a,a)}=B(u,w)$, using symmetry. Since $B(a,a)
e0$ the functional $B(-,a)$ is nonzero, so by rank-nullity ([[thm-rank-nullity]], [[def-dimension]]) its kernel has dimension $\dim V-1$, i.e. is a hyperplane ([[def-linear-subspace]]). (3) In the basis $(e_s,e_t)$ one has $r_s(e_s)=-e_s$, $r_s(e_t)=e_t+2ce_s$ and $r_t(e_t)=-e_t$, $r_t(e_s)=e_s+2ce_t$; matrix multiplication ([[def-coordinate-column-and-matrix-of-a-linear-map]], [[thm-matrix-of-a-composite-is-the-product]]) gives the displayed $A$ with $\det A=(4c^2-1)(-1)-(-2c)(2c)=1$. The quadratic form is the square-sum displayed in (i); for finite $m$, $1-c^2=\sin^2(\pi/m)>0$ because $\sin(\pi/m)
e0$ for $m\ge2$ ([[cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity]], [[thm-sine-cosine-zero-sets-and-fundamental-period]]), so $B|_P$ is positive definite; for $m=\infty$, $c=1$ and the form is $(x_s-x_t)^2$ with radical $\mathbb R(e_s+e_t)$. For finite $m$ the Gram matrix is invertible, so solving the $2	imes2$ system $B(p,e_s)=B(v,e_s)$, $B(p,e_t)=B(v,e_t)$ for $p\in P$ and putting $z=v-p$ presents every $v$ as $p+z$ with $z\in P^\perp$; positive definiteness gives $P\cap P^\perp=0$, so $V=P\oplus P^\perp$ ([[def-internal-direct-sum]], [[lem-direct-sum-criterion]]), and $r_s,r_t$ fix $P^\perp$ pointwise by the fixed-hyperplane formula in (2). For the order: $\operatorname{tr}A=4c^2-2=2(2c^2-1)=2\cos(2\pi/m)$ by the double-angle formula, so the $2	imes2$ Cayley–Hamilton identity (verified by direct computation) gives $A^2=2\cos(2\pi/m)A-I$; induction using $2\sin x\cos y=\sin(x+y)+\sin(x-y)$ from the addition formulas gives $A^k= rac{\sin(2k\pi/m)A-\sin(2(k-1)\pi/m)I}{\sin(2\pi/m)}$ for $k\ge1$, and $A^m=I$. Since $2c
e0$ for $m\ge3$, $A$ is not a scalar matrix, so $A^k=I$ forces $\sin(2k\pi/m)=0$, hence $2k\pi/m\in\pi\mathbb Z$ and then $\sin(2(k-1)\pi/m)=-\sin(2\pi/m)$ forces $m\mid k$: the order is exactly $m$. The case $m=2$ is direct: $c=\cos(\pi/2)=0$ and $A=-I$ has order $2$. For $m=\infty$, $c=1$, $A= egin{pmatrix}3&-2\2&-1\end{pmatrix}=I+N$ with $N= egin{pmatrix}2&-2\2&-2\end{pmatrix}
e0$ and $N^2=0$; the binomial theorem gives $A^k=I+kN$ for $k\ge0$ and $A^{-1}=I-N$, and $kN
e0$ for $k
e0$ because $\mathbb R$ has characteristic zero (`2
e0`). No Choice is used anywhere: every step is a finite computation or a finite-dimensional dimension count.

items.title: The canonical reflection homomorphism, roots, reflections, and the positive cone
items.statement:
Let $S$, $m$, $V$, $B$ be as in [[def-cg-real-coxeter-form-and-reflection]], let $W$ be the presented Coxeter group of [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]] with its universal property, and put $r_s:=r_{e_s}$ for $s\in S$ ([[lem-cg-reflection-form-invariance-and-rank-two-orders]]).

**(1)** Write $\mathrm{GL}(V)$ for the group of invertible linear maps $V\to V$, the unit group of the monoid of linear endomorphisms under composition ([[def-linear-isomorphism-and-invertible-linear-map]], [[def-vector-space-of-linear-maps]], [[lem-composition-and-identity-linear-maps]], [[lem-monoid-units-form-a-group]]). The **canonical reflection homomorphism** is the group homomorphism $\rho:W\to\mathrm{GL}(V)$ ([[def-group-homomorphism]]) that satisfies $\rho(s)=r_s$ for every $s\in S$; its existence and uniqueness are established by [[lem-cg-reflection-representation-descends-and-root-norms]], which is this definition's recorded justifier. For $w\in W$ and $v\in V$ write $\rho(w)v$ for the image.

**(2)** The **root system** of the pair is $\Phi:=\{\rho(w)e_s:w\in W,\ s\in S\}\subset V$; its elements are the **roots**. The set of **reflections** of $W$ is $T:=\{wsw^{-1}:w\in W,\ s\in S\}\subset W$; that $\rho(wsw^{-1})$ is the reflection $r_{\rho(w)e_s}$ and that every root is $B$-non-isotropic are proved in [[lem-cg-reflection-representation-descends-and-root-norms]].

**(3)** The **positive cone** is $V_+:=\{\sum_{s\in S}\lambda_se_s:\lambda_s\in\mathbb R,\ \lambda_s\ge0\}$ and the **negative cone** is $-V_+$ ([[def-linear-combination-and-span]]).

No positivity of $\rho(w)e_s$ for fixed $w$, no faithfulness or injectivity of $\rho$, no discreteness and no nondegeneracy of $B$ is asserted by this definition.
items.strategy: A definition item. Every symbol names an object already constructed: $V$, $B$, the $e_s$ and $r_s$ come from the previous items of this page, and $W$ with its presentation and universal property comes from [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]]; $\rho$ is defined by its values on the generating set $S$, and the well-definedness obligation (that the generator assignment satisfies the presentation's relators, so that the universal property yields a unique homomorphism) is exactly what the recorded justifier [[lem-cg-reflection-representation-descends-and-root-norms]] proves. $\Phi$, $T$, $V_+$ and $-V_+$ are set definitions, and the membership of roots in the non-isotropic locus, and the identification $\rho(wsw^{-1})=r_{\rho(w)e_s}$, are attributed to the justifier rather than asserted here. The stated abstentions (no positivity, faithfulness, discreteness or nondegeneracy) preserve the design's warning that these are conclusions of later pages, not part of this definition. No Choice is used.

items.title: Descent of the reflection representation, unit root norms, and conjugation of reflections
items.statement:
Let $S$, $m$, $V$, $B$, $W$, $r_s$, $\rho$, $\Phi$, $T$ be as in [[def-cg-canonical-reflection-homomorphism]].

**(1) Relators and descent.** For every $s\in S$ one has $r_s^2=\mathrm{id}_V$, and for all $s\ne t$ with $m(s,t)<\infty$ one has $(r_sr_t)^{m(s,t)}=\mathrm{id}_V$. Consequently the assignment $s\mapsto r_s$ sends every relator of the presentation to the identity, and by the universal property of [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]] there is a **unique** group homomorphism $\rho:W\to\mathrm{GL}(V)$ with $\rho(s)=r_s$ for all $s\in S$.

**(2) $\rho$ preserves the form.** For every $w\in W$ and all $u,w'\in V$, $B(\rho(w)u,\rho(w)w')=B(u,w')$.

**(3) Roots have unit norm.** For every $w\in W$ and $s\in S$, $B(\rho(w)e_s,\rho(w)e_s)=1$; hence every root $\alpha\in\Phi$ satisfies $B(\alpha,\alpha)=1\ne0$ and $r_\alpha$ is defined.

**(4) Conjugation of reflections.** Let $g\in\mathrm{GL}(V)$ be $B$-preserving and let $a\in V$ with $B(a,a)\ne0$. Then $gr_ag^{-1}=r_{ga}$. In particular, for every $w\in W$ and $s\in S$, $$\rho(wsw^{-1})=\rho(w)r_s\rho(w)^{-1}=r_{\rho(w)e_s},$$ so every $t=wsw^{-1}\in T$ acts on $V$ as the reflection in the root $\rho(w)e_s\in\Phi$.
items.strategy: (1) $r_s^2=\mathrm{id}$ and $B$-invariance of each $r_s$ are [[lem-cg-reflection-form-invariance-and-rank-two-orders]] (2); the exact rank-two orders give $(r_sr_t)^{m(s,t)}=\mathrm{id}$. These are precisely the relators of the presented group, so the map $S\to\mathrm{GL}(V)$, $s\mapsto r_s$ satisfies the hypotheses of the universal property ([[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]]), which yields a homomorphism $\rho$; uniqueness holds because $S$ generates $W$ ([[def-generated-subgroup]]). (2) Each generator preserves $B$, and a composite of $B$-preserving maps preserves $B$. (3) $B(\rho(w)e_s,\rho(w)e_s)=B(e_s,e_s)=1$ by (2) and $B(e_s,e_s)=1$. (4) Let $g$ preserve $B$. Then $B(ga,ga)=B(a,a)$ and $B(g^{-1}v,a)=B(v,ga)$, so $r_{ga}(v)=v-\frac{2B(g^{-1}v,a)}{B(a,a)}ga=g\bigl(g^{-1}v-\frac{2B(g^{-1}v,a)}{B(a,a)}a\bigr)=gr_ag^{-1}(v)$ for all $v$; substituting $g=\rho(w)$, $a=e_s$ and using $\rho(s)=r_s$ gives the displayed conjugation identity. No Choice is used.

items.title: The dual action, chambers, faces, and root hyperplanes
items.statement:
Let $S$, $m$, $V$, $B$, $W$, $\rho$, $\Phi$ be as in [[def-cg-canonical-reflection-homomorphism]], and let $V^*$ be the algebraic dual of $V$ ([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]).

**(1) The dual action.** For $w\in W$ and $f\in V^*$ define $w\cdot f\in V^*$ by $$(w\cdot f)(v):=f(\rho(w)^{-1}v).$$ This is the dual (contragredient) action of $\rho$; that it really is a left action by linear maps is proved in [[lem-cg-dual-action-and-chamber-faces-exist]]. **The dual action is used even when $B$ is degenerate**: no identification of $V$ with $V^*$ through $B$ is made or assumed.

**(2) Chambers, faces, root hyperplanes.** The **closed chamber** is $C:=\{f\in V^*:f(e_s)\ge0\text{ for all }s\in S\}$, its **interior** is $C^\circ:=\{f\in V^*:f(e_s)>0\text{ for all }s\in S\}$, and for $I\subseteq S$ the **face** $C_I$ is $$C_I:=\{f\in V^*:f(e_s)=0\text{ for }s\in I\text{ and }f(e_s)>0\text{ for }s\notin I\},$$ the set of functionals of $C$ vanishing exactly on $I$. For a root $\alpha\in\Phi$ the **root hyperplane** is $H_\alpha:=\{f\in V^*:f(\alpha)=0\}=\ker(\mathrm{ev}_\alpha)$, the kernel of the evaluation functional $f\mapsto f(\alpha)$ ([[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]).

Neither the nonemptiness of the $C_I$ nor any orbit or tiling property is asserted here; existence of the faces and the exact rank-two chamber structure are proved in [[lem-cg-dual-action-and-chamber-faces-exist]].
items.strategy: A definition item. $V^*$ is the published algebraic dual ([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]); since $\rho(w)$ is invertible ([[lem-cg-reflection-representation-descends-and-root-norms]]), the formula $(w\cdot f)(v)=f(\rho(w)^{-1}v)$ defines an element of $V^*$ for each $w,f$, and the action axioms are not asserted but delegated to the recorded justifier [[lem-cg-dual-action-and-chamber-faces-exist]]. The closed chamber $C$ and its faces are the standard Tits-cone chamber of the dual (geometric) representation (Davis Appendix D.1); the root hyperplanes are the kernels of the evaluation functionals at roots (a hyperplane is the kernel of a nonzero functional, [[def-linear-subspace]], [[def-kernel-and-image-of-a-linear-map]]). The design's explicit warning is kept: the dual action is required even when $B$ is degenerate, so no isomorphism $V\cong V^*$ induced by $B$ is used. No Choice is used.

items.title: The dual action, the faces, and the rank-two chamber tiling
items.statement:
With the notation of [[def-cg-dual-chambers-and-reflection-hyperplanes]]:

**(1) The dual action is an action by linear maps.** For all $w_1,w_2\in W$ and $f\in V^*$ one has $\mathrm{id}\cdot f=f$ and $w_1\cdot(w_2\cdot f)=(w_1w_2)\cdot f$, and for each $w$ the map $f\mapsto w\cdot f$ is linear.

**(2) The faces are nonempty.** Let $f_s\in V^*$ be the dual basis functionals of the basis $(e_s)$ of $V$, i.e. $f_s(e_t)=\delta_{st}$ ([[def-dual-family-associated-to-a-basis]], [[thm-dual-family-is-a-basis-in-finite-dimension]]). For $I\subseteq S$ the functional $f_I:=\sum_{s\notin I}f_s$ satisfies $f_I(e_s)=1$ for $s\notin I$ and $f_I(e_s)=0$ for $s\in I$; hence $f_I\in C_I$ and every face is nonempty. In particular $C^\circ\ni\sum_{s\in S}f_s$ is nonempty and $C_S=\{0\}$.

**(3) Rank two.** Let $s\ne t$ in $S$ and put $P:=\mathbb Re_s+\mathbb Re_t$. Let $P^*:=\mathrm{Hom}(P,\mathbb R)$ be the algebraic dual space of the $2$-dimensional space $P$ ([[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]), with the dual basis $f_s,f_t$ of the basis $(e_s,e_t)$ of $P$; functionals on $P$ are the restrictions of functionals on $V$. Let $W_{s,t}:=\langle\rho(s),\rho(t)\rangle\subseteq\mathrm{GL}(V)$ be the matrix subgroup generated by the two reflections. It preserves $P$. For $g\in W_{s,t}$ and $\varphi\in P^*$ define $(g\cdot\varphi)(v):=\varphi(g^{-1}v)$ for $v\in P$; this is a left action of $W_{s,t}$ on $P^*$ by linear maps, the contragredient of its restriction to $P$. The abstract subgroup $\langle s,t\rangle\le W$ acts through its image $W_{s,t}$; no action of all of $W$ on $P^*$ is asserted. Writing $c:=c(s,t)$ (so $c=1$ for $m(s,t)=\infty$) and coordinates $(y_s,y_t)$ on $P^*$, so that $\varphi=y_sf_s+y_tf_t$ and $\varphi(e_s)=y_s$, $\varphi(e_t)=y_t$, the dual generators act by $$\rho(s)^*(y_s,y_t)=(-y_s,\ 2cy_s+y_t),\qquad \rho(t)^*(y_s,y_t)=(y_s+2cy_t,\ -y_t);$$ each is an involution fixing the line $\{\varphi:\varphi(e_s)=0\}=\{y_s=0\}$ pointwise, respectively $\{\varphi:\varphi(e_t)=0\}=\{y_t=0\}$, and the functional $\delta(\varphi):=\varphi(e_s+e_t)$ is preserved by $W_{s,t}$ when $m(s,t)=\infty$. Put $\Phi_P:=W_{s,t}\{e_s,e_t\}\subset P$, the rank-two root system. For $\beta\in\Phi_P$ the rank-two root hyperplane is $H_\beta\cap P^*:=\{\varphi\in P^*:\varphi(\beta)=0\}$.

(i) If $m:=m(s,t)<\infty$: $W_{s,t}$ is a dihedral group of order $2m$, and the $2m$ chambers $wC_P$ ($w\in W_{s,t}$), where $C_P:=\{f\in P^*:f(e_s)\ge0,\ f(e_t)\ge0\}$, are exactly the $2m$ closed sectors cut out in $P^*$ by the $m$ root hyperplanes $H_\beta\cap P^*$ $(\beta\in\Phi_P)$, $\Phi_P:=W_{s,t}\{e_s,e_t\}$. They have pairwise disjoint interiors, their union is all of $P^*$, $W_{s,t}$ acts simply transitively on them, and any two distinct chambers are separated by at least one root hyperplane, i.e. there is $\beta\in\Phi_P$ with the two interiors in opposite open half-planes of $H_\beta$.

(ii) If $m(s,t)=\infty$: the chambers $wC_P$ ($w\in W_{s,t}$) have pairwise disjoint interiors and their union is $\{\varphi\in P^*:\varphi(e_s+e_t)>0\}\cup\{0\}$, that is, the closed half-plane $\{\varphi:\varphi(e_s+e_t)\ge0\}$ with the nonzero points of its boundary line removed; any two distinct chambers are separated by at least one root hyperplane $H_\beta\cap P^*$ $(\beta\in\Phi_P)$, and the traces $H_\beta\cap\{\varphi:\varphi(e_s+e_t)=1\}$ are exactly the integers in the coordinate $y_s$ on that affine line.
items.strategy: Prove the inverse-composition left action and finite dual-basis face witnesses; norm 1 and coordinate evaluation, then rank-nullity, give root hyperplanes (1.1-1.3). Build the finite orthonormal rank-two model and rotation (1.4); enumerate all four finite root families to get 2m roots (2.1). In the infinite case use normal forms, exact affine interval images, lem-integer-part for coverage, and four integer-coordinate root families for exhaustive wall traces (2.2), proving delta>0 union {0}. For finite m give flat an explicit inverse and equivariance (3.1); prove the matrix subgroup has order 2m, enumerate the base sector and its reflection under rotation, and separate interiors by signs of wall forms (4.1). Restrict root hyperplanes to beta in Phi_P and the P^* action to the invariant-plane subgroup. No Choice is used; retain the Davis closed-half-plane source caveat.

title: Real Forms and Reflection Geometry — Examples

items.title: Reflection matrices in a positive plane, a Lorentzian plane, and a plane with radical
items.statement:
Let $B$ be a symmetric bilinear form on a real vector space $V$ and let $a\in V$ with $B(a,a)\ne0$. Define $r_a(v):=v-2B(v,a)a/B(a,a)$, using the same formula as [[def-cg-real-coxeter-form-and-reflection]]. Step 1.1 below proves directly that this is a linear involution preserving $B$ and fixing $\ker B(-,a)$ pointwise for this general $B$. In the three cases take $V=\mathbb R^2$, whose functions have domain $\{0,1\}$ ([[def-function-space]]), and relabel coordinates by $x_1:=x(0)$, $x_2:=x(1)$ and standard unit vectors by $e_1,e_2$, respectively ([[lem-standard-basis-of-f-n]]). Each matrix is taken in the ordered basis $(e_1,e_2)$; inertia is as in [[def-definiteness-inertia-and-signature-data-over-the-reals]].

**(i) Positive plane.** $B$ the dot product, $a=\frac35e_1+\frac45e_2$, so $B(a,a)=1$. Then $r_a(e_1)=\frac7{25}e_1-\frac{24}{25}e_2$, $r_a(e_2)=-\frac{24}{25}e_1-\frac7{25}e_2$, i.e. $$[r_a]=\frac1{25}\begin{pmatrix}7&-24\\-24&-7\end{pmatrix},\qquad [r_a]^2=I_2,\qquad \det[r_a]=-1,$$ and $B$ has inertia $(2,0,0)$: a Euclidean reflection across the line $\mathbb R(-4e_1+3e_2)$.

**(ii) Lorentzian plane.** $B(x,y)=x_1y_1-x_2y_2$, of inertia $(1,1,0)$, and $a=2e_1+e_2$, so $B(a,a)=3$. Then $r_a(e_1)=-\frac53e_1-\frac43e_2$, $r_a(e_2)=\frac43e_1+\frac53e_2$, i.e. $$[r_a]=\frac13\begin{pmatrix}-5&4\\-4&5\end{pmatrix},\qquad [r_a]^2=I_2,\qquad \det[r_a]=-1,$$ and $[r_a]$ preserves $B$: $B(r_ae_1,r_ae_1)=1$, $B(r_ae_2,r_ae_2)=-1$, $B(r_ae_1,r_ae_2)=0$.

**(iii) Plane with radical.** $B(x,y)=x_1y_1$, of inertia $(1,0,1)$ and radical $\operatorname{rad}(B)=\mathbb Re_2$ ([[def-matrix-radicals-rank-and-nondegeneracy-of-a-bilinear-form]]), and $a=e_1$: then $r_a=\mathrm{diag}(-1,1)$, i.e. $r_a(e_1)=-e_1$ and $r_a(e_2)=e_2$, with fixed hyperplane $\ker B(-,e_1)=\mathbb Re_2=\operatorname{rad}(B)$. The vector $e_2$ is $B$-null, so the displayed formula does not define a reflection with normal $e_2$.
items.strategy: First prove locally for an arbitrary symmetric real B and nonzero d=B(a,a) that the displayed map is linear, involutive, B-preserving, negates a and has exactly ker B(-,a) as fixed set (Verification 1.1). Relabel the function coordinates 0,1 as 1,2. Compute the positive, Lorentzian and radical matrices, squares, determinants, Gram values, inertia and fixed kernels in 2.1-2.3; conclude in 3.1. The Coxeter-specific lemma is not invoked for arbitrary B. No Choice is used.

items.title: The finite dihedral rotation and the infinite unipotent rank-two product
items.statement:
Let $S=\{s,t\}$, $m=m(s,t)$, $V=\mathbb R^S$, $B$ the Coxeter form, $P=\mathbb Re_s+\mathbb Re_t$ and $c$ as in [[def-cg-real-coxeter-form-and-reflection]] ($c=1$ for $m=\infty$). By [[lem-cg-reflection-form-invariance-and-rank-two-orders]] the product $A:=r_sr_t$ acts on $P$ with matrix $$A=\begin{pmatrix}4c^2-1&-2c\\2c&-1\end{pmatrix}$$ in the basis $(e_s,e_t)$ ([[def-coordinate-column-and-matrix-of-a-linear-map]]).

**(i) Finite dihedral rotation.** For $m=3$ one has $c=\cos(\pi/3)=\frac12$ and $$A=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad A^2=\begin{pmatrix}-1&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad A^3=I_2,$$ so $A$ has order $3=m$; its trace is $-1=2\cos(2\pi/3)$, consistent with a rotation through $2\pi/3$ of the positive definite plane $(P,B|_P)$, and $A\ne I_2\ne A^2$. For $m=2$ the same formula gives $c=0$ and $A=-I_2$, of order $2=m$.

**(ii) Infinite unipotent product.** For $m=\infty$ one has $c=1$ and $$A=\begin{pmatrix}3&-2\\2&-1\end{pmatrix}=I_2+N,\qquad N=\begin{pmatrix}2&-2\\2&-2\end{pmatrix}\ne0,\qquad N^2=0 .$$ Hence $A^k=I_2+kN$ for every $k\in\mathbb Z$, so $A^k(e_s)=e_s+2k(e_s+e_t)$ and no nonzero power of $A$ is the identity: the product $r_sr_t$ has infinite order, in contrast to the finite cases where $A$ has order $m$. In the abstract group $W$ of [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]], the element $st$ likewise has infinite order when $m=\infty$, and has order $m$ in the displayed finite cases $m=2,3$.

All assertions are explicit matrix computations. For $m=3$, $\cos(\pi/3)= rac12$ is derived from $\cos\pi=-1$ ([[thm-quarter-turn-values-and-shift-formulas]]) and the triple-angle identity $\cos3x=4\cos^3x-3\cos x$ obtained from the addition formulas ([[thm-sine-and-cosine-addition-formulas]]): $4c^3-3c+1=(c+1)(2c-1)^2$, and $c

Substituting $c= rac12$ gives the displayed matrices and the powers $A^2$, $A^3$ are computed by matrix multiplication ([[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]]). For $m=\infty$, substituting $c=1$ gives $A=I_2+N$; $N^2=0$ is checked directly, the binomial expansion gives $A^k=I_2+kN$ for $k\ge0$, and $A^{-1}=I_2-N$ gives the identity for $k<0$; $kN
e0$ for $k

To transfer the displayed orders to the abstract group, use the proved involutions and the finite pair relation of the rank-two lemma to apply the presentation universal property in [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]]. The resulting homomorphism sends $st$ to $A$.
